title: Utah Residents Protest Data Centers at Planning Commission Meeting in Provo

tea.why: Residents opposed proposed zoning ordinance changes allowing new data centers due to concerns over heavy water and electricity demands.
tea.want: Reject the proposed data center zoning ordinance and halt facility construction approvals.
tea.changed: Oct 22: Sheriff's deputies arrested three people during the meeting, leading to online public backlash and calls for officer termination.

summary: Scores of residents gathered at a Utah County Planning Commission meeting in Provo to protest proposed land use amendments that would allow data centers in mining, grazing, and industrial zones. Attendees expressed concerns regarding the high water and electricity demands of data facilities. During the meeting, a physical altercation occurred when law enforcement attempted to remove a protester from the room. Video footage showed a deputy taking the woman to the ground, resulting in her arrest alongside two others. The Utah County Sheriff’s Office stated that deputies attempted to escort the individual out after she argued and refused to leave, alleging she struck an officer. The protester disputed the allegation and stated she suffered a concussion and bruises, prompting widespread public backlash and demands for the deputy's dismissal.
demands: Reject proposed data center zoning changes
Protect local water and electricity resources from massive facility demands
Fire the deputy involved in the physical restraint of the protester
response: The Utah County Sheriff’s Office stated deputies tried to escort a woman out after she argued and refused to leave, alleging she struck a deputy in the groin. updates.text: Residents protested data center regulations at the Utah County Planning Commission meeting in Provo, leading to three arrests.
The Utah County Sheriff's Office released a statement defending the deputy's actions and detailing the charges against the arrested individuals.
Viral video of the arrest sparked intense public backlash online, with the injured protester calling for the involved deputy to be fired.
